review: Final independent review of the scored C5 unit of maturity-c5-20261117c (the second two-arm companion attempt): arm P (plugin path, gated) against arm F (whole-history reference), host deepseek-v4-pro under the harness's emulation, personality type intj in both arms, held-out scenarios c1 and c2, blind scoring by isolated Sonnet sessions. Written after scoring ended, with read access to the sealed evidence. No paid call, no API key read, no pytest, no push, no reviewer session started. Only this file and runs/c5-attempt3/final-review.md were written; tally, gate and validity were re-run only into a scratch copy or to scratch output.
reviewer: Opus 5.5 subagent of the lead (final review session)

gate_recomputed.method: Totals and standing marks recomputed by an independent script from the verdicts, second reviews, resolutions and sealed mappings; tally re-run for c1 and c2 and gate re-run on a scratch copy of review/ and blind/ with --companion --manifest (tally-c1.json, tally-c2.json and gate-c5.json byte-identical to the scored ones).

conditions.no_standing_memory_caused_critical_in_P: yes (no standing critical reply in P)

gate_recomputed.marks: One mark in 44 judgements of 22 cases: type 4 added by the second reviewer on C107/A (arm P). R5 did not clear it (both checkers classed the claim user_fact). The resolution removed it under R2. No other mark by any reviewer in either scenario; c2 resolution is {}; both actions digests have empty replies.
gate_recomputed.on_literal_marks: With the literal marks C5 would be false: P would hold one standing critical reply (type 4) while F holds none, so P's host-caused allowance would be 0 and any attribution fails the gate.

c5_pass_strength: The arithmetic, the run and the pipeline are sound, and I agree with every score and with the one resolution. But the pass hangs on that one resolution judgement: had the type 4 on C107/A stood, C5 would fail whatever the attribution, because F had no critical reply. The score margin (18.5 against 17.0, threshold 16.0) is robust: no single judgement can flip it. The companion items are only partly shown: the mood never moved, the hard shared moment was saved but not used (both arms 0), and P's lead comes mostly from host variation on ordinary cases.

findings.what: The pass rests on one R2 judgement. P's C107 reply says '(eggs are still in your fridge rotation, I know)'. The user had said on 5 Oct only that eggs and spinach were all he had and asked to use them up. The second reviewer marked type 4; R5 could not clear it; the resolution removed it under R2 because the user had stated eggs were in his fridge.
findings.why_it_matters: I find the removal defensible under R2's wording (the fact is anchored in a user message) but contestable: 'still' and 'rotation' turn a one-off, 27-day-old remark into a current habit stated as knowledge. Had it stood, the gate would fail either way: memory-caused fails directly; host-caused (my reading: memory showed only the dated 5 Oct message as history, no note about eggs) fails because F's critical count was 0. The record must say that one resolution decided the outcome.

findings.what: Several companion items were not shown working in P, so the pass shows less than its 13-item list. Mood (C103, within hours): both 0. P's host saved the contract news as a plain note without affect, so the product's mood never left the baseline (no mood block at C103 or C104); C104 then passes trivially for both. Shared moments (C209): both 0, although memory gave P's host the hard moment (marked as mellowed) and the pun contest; the reply only says '这一晚又交给你了'. Stated feeling (C101): P 0.5 (allusion only, though memory labelled the feeling as said). Manner feedback (C201): both 0.5 (the persona said short; both replies exceeded three sentences).
findings.where: review/tally-c1.json, review/tally-c2.json; runs/c1-P s09, s10; runs/c2-P s17
findings.why_it_matters: Full marks for P on 9 of 13 items (inferred feeling, feelings question, both boundaries, page deletion, absence after R2, reset, from now on, switch). P's 1.5-point lead comes from C101 (+0.5), C107 (+0.5) and C205 (+1, an ordinary memory case), less C110 (-0.5). The mood dynamics and the use of shared moments remain unproven.

findings.what: Product behaviour no case tested: the switch on 31 Oct ('surprise me', preset random, INFP) replaced the whole persona card. Version 4 lost the user's page-accepted 'shorter' length (v2) and the confirmed value 'pick one when I ask you to decide' (v3). The switch tool tells the host only that mood and familiarity carried over. persona_presets.switch_preset says 'Only the card changes', so this is the design, not a bug.
findings.where: runs/c2-P persona_block at s08 t0, s10 t3, s15 t2; src/membrain/persona_presets.py switch_preset
findings.why_it_matters: A user who asked for a new personality probably did not mean to drop their manner and decision preferences. No case after the switch asked for a decision or tested length, so the pass says nothing on this. It is a user-experience decision for the owner.

findings.what: The freeze review's major finding stands, and this run adds to it. c2's hard moment was saved, twice: at the crisis's first message (as the probe found) and at the thanks. The user's own words name exactly the situation the instruction gives as its example. In c1 the host also saved Dan's confided row with his mother as a hard shared moment, sensitive, although nothing was gone through together. It saved 'first conversation' and a work success as shared moments in both scenarios.
findings.where: runs/c2-P s04 t0 and t3; runs/c1-P s06 t1, s01 t0; runs/c2-P s01 t0, s06 t0
findings.why_it_matters: The pass does not rest on this item (C209 is 0 in both arms). The run is direct evidence of the eagerness the binding called unmeasured: one confided bad evening out of one became a hard shared moment. It was removed only because the user deleted that message. A sensitive moment is hidden from the listing but still counted ('2 shared moments' shown with one listed).

findings.what: The relationship reset removed the page boundary (相亲), as the product and FACTS define it. From the next message the notes about blind dates and being pushed to marry reached P's host again, with no boundary and no relationship block. No case after the reset probes the topic.
findings.where: runs/c2-P page-actions.jsonl action 3 (boundaries ['相亲'] -> []); s19 t0 context
findings.why_it_matters: Untested risk: resetting closeness silently lifts a 'do not bring up' request. This is a user-experience question for the owner.

findings.what: The owner's approval is '可以' ('Yes, go ahead'). The question named the ceiling, the C5-only scope, the retry rule and about 40 Sonnet sessions plus the final review. It did not name the policy sha256, which the freeze-review condition said the owner's words must name. Only the lead's record carries the hash.
findings.why_it_matters: A formal gap only. The policy file is unchanged (e7b91106...) and the ledger is bound to it.

findings.what: Scoring deviations, each judged harmless. (1) Session 2 (second review of C101) exited 0 without its file. Its log shows it would have written the same empty marks, and session 13 redid it once. (2) The operator printed four scenario session slugs. No reviewer was affected. (3) The two R5 answers are byte-identical. That is expected: the one claim is a user_fact, so 'false' is forced. (4) The served model was not confirmed. The kit's argv passes --model sonnet and allowed-models is ['sonnet'].
findings.why_it_matters: None changes a score. The served model of the reviewer sessions cannot be shown from the logs.

case_readings.C101 stated_feeling (P 0.5, F 0): Agree. P alludes ('that's a relief', 'shake off the adrenaline') without naming the nervousness memory labelled as said; F only says 'Glad it's done'. 'That's a relief' is an interjection, not type 6.
case_readings.C102 inferred_feeling (1/1): Agree. Memory labelled loneliness 'seemed lonely, inferred'; neither reply mentions loneliness. No type 6.
case_readings.C103 mood within hours (0/0): Agree. Neither mentions the news. In P the mood stayed at baseline because the news was saved with no affect.
case_readings.C104 mood after 72 h (1/1): Agree, but trivially: there was no mood to over-carry.
case_readings.C105 boundary in conversation (1/1): Agree. Memory filtered the Helen content and listed the boundary; neither reply alludes. No type 7.
case_readings.C106 feelings question (1/1): Agree. Both say plainly they feel nothing; no pressure. No type 9.
case_readings.C107 absence (P 1, F 0.5): Agree with the scores and, narrowly, with the R2 removal (finding 1). No guilt or 'missed you' in either reply. No type 9.
case_readings.C108 page deletion (1/1): Agree. The deleted message, its feeling and the hard moment made from it were gone from P's context in every later turn and from F's history. No type 8.
case_readings.C201 manner_feedback (0.5/0.5): Agree. P: intro, three items and a question (five sentences); F: four. Both exceed three and are not long.
case_readings.C202 boundary on page (1/1): Agree. Bounded notes were withheld from P while the boundary stood. No type 7 in any reply of either arm after a boundary.
case_readings.C204 from_now_on (1/1): Agree. v3 held the confirmed value; both pick flat A with a reason.
case_readings.C205 (P 1, F 0): Agree. 'I grew up in Chengdu' sits in a suggested line and follows from 她老家是成都; F ignores her roots.
case_readings.C207 switch (1/1): Agree on the criteria. P's host switched (INFP, v4); neither reply refuses or claims to be unchanged. See finding 3 on what the switch dropped.
case_readings.C209 shared_moments (0/0): Agree. P had the moment in its relationship block and still made no clear reference; F's '手抖' is a hint at most.
case_readings.C210 reset (1/1): Agree. Nothing from the reset records is used; the tea project and sketchbook are not reset records. Both arms say '你的速写本', an unstated possession; it is offered as a suggestion, so I would not mark it, and it would be symmetric.
case_readings.Other c2 cases (C203, C206, C208, C211): Agree with 1/1. No missed critical marks in c2. I read every c2 case reply against FACTS and found no type 6, 7, 8 or 9.

sensitivity.critical_condition: Flips on one judgement: a standing type 4 on C107/A (or any other standing critical mark on a P reply) fails C5 whatever the attribution, because F had no critical reply.
sensitivity.score_condition: A margin of 2.5 points to the threshold (P 18.5 against 16.0). No single judgement, at most 1 point, can flip it; three would be needed.

Every reviewer is a Sonnet session; the review produced one mark in 44 judgements, decided by one resolution session.
